summary: Tony tests Gemini 4 Argon against other LLMs using an agent benchmark prompt to build an animated 3D night train crossing a bridge.
summaryEn: Benchmark comparison of Gemini 4 Argon generating an animated 3D night train scene

post.originalText:
Gemini 4 Argon vs Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs Gpt 6 Astra vs Opus 5.5  

Same prompt: "Build a night train."

What do you guys think? 👀 https://t.co/VH5ymsCaIs

sourceMaterials.text: @idyeahstudio The zoom is unforgiving 😂 That’s why a single screenshot only tells part of the story with these scenes.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @gupta_pranjal Yep, on this run 😅 $5.53 for Opus versus $18.80 for Sonnet. I’m comparing the total cost of completing the task here.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @MeDusa7768 That red locomotive has character 😅 I like the result too, though I’d struggle to justify the extra spend over Opus here.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@gupta_pranjal I can see the case for Sonnet’s locomotive 👀 

For value, I’d still pick Opus here: $5.53 versus $18.80 is a big gap.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @kasparite 🤣 i can DM you the entire prompt if you want too. I don't think it was a good idea to put it all in this post 😂
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @manxlab Exactly! I think it can just keep improving without limits. That's why Opus 5.5 is my go-to.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev
EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@manxlab Sonnet took the scenic route 😂 

I like its locomotive, but 2h40 and $18.80 is a tough sell beside these other results.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@MMaximalux The writing style matters when you’re going back and forth all day 😅 

Clear explanations are part of what makes a model comfortable to work with.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @MMaximalux Still my main model too 😅 But Argon getting this close in four minutes makes me curious how it would handle my everyday coding tasks.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@furkan_akin25 Yeah, especially the blue locomotive and forest 👀 

Opus feels moodier to me, while Argon’s brighter lighting makes the bridge and mountains stand out.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@Eliopyr That’s what I like about showing the results 🙌 

You can disagree with my pick and still get something useful from the comparison.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @rubenssoto_ai I mean for the price, I'll stick to Opus 5.5 for sure !
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev
EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @web3_scholar_ Fair 😄 Astra’s steam train, Sonnet’s detailing, Argon’s brighter palette and Opus’s atmosphere each give people something different to like.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @TonyyRickk Yep 👀 The differences in locomotive style and lighting make the comparison fun, even before looking at time and cost.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@nivlek_smada The replies show that nicely 🙌 

Some people focus on the locomotive detail, others the atmosphere, and others the time and cost.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text: @reymond______ Right 😂 We’re already debating the lighting and trees like asking an agent to build an animated 3D train scene is completely normal.
sourceMaterials.author: EnvolDev

sourceMaterials.text:
@jpshrodinger Argon’s blue palette looks good here 👀 

Getting that result in 4m20s gives it a strong case on value.
